Class 11 Chemistry · Chemical bonding
Chemistry, visualised #10

Sodium is the metal that explodes in water. Chlorine was a poison gas in World War 1.
Watch what happens when they meet, and what one electron does.
Then a second question: why does one liquid light the bulb and the other doesn't?
Ionic bonding comes up in JEE Main, NEET and MHT-CET.

Atoms zoomed in about 50 million times (their sizes are true to each other); the ions in the beaker are drawn far bigger than real. A sealed lab demo: never try it.
